Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the planning fee share, the smallest fee, the markup, the target margin, the reserve and the owner approval limit.
Check Events: contract value, planned, agreed and actual cost, guests and status. The margin, the cost per guest and the plan check fill in by themselves.
Enter or check every category on Budget Lines. The variance to plan, the cost per guest and the over plan flag fill in.
Keep Category Share Guide, Per-guest Cost Guide, Guest Count Bands and Markup by Category current: they answer how much a new event should cost.
Use Catering Menus, Venue Pricing, Vendor Price List and Extras Price List to price a proposal, and Season Price Index to see how the month moves the price.
Record every quote on Quote Comparison and mark the one chosen. The saving against the highest quote and the rank fill in.
Record every change after signing on Budget Changes and every saved version on Budget Versions. Changes above your limit are flagged for the owner.
Write each use of the reserve on Contingency Use and each change of the head count on Guest Count Changes. The reserve left and the lock check fill in.
Log team hours on Event Hours, keep Labour Allowance and Planning Fee Schedule up to date and read the fee per hour on Events.
Enter every tasting on Tasting Costs: the costs you did not bill to the client are flagged.

Use the 14 calculators before you quote: budget by guest count, catering, venues, guest changes, markup, price per guest, staff, rentals, bar, overrun, reserve, fee yield, two quotes and a what-if grid.
Read Event Budget Dashboard and Charts every week: margin, overruns, reserve used, guest count changes, labour hours and savings from quotes.
Book the right vendors and pay them on time, every event
Vendor bookings, payments, quotes and holds for event planners
Deposit and balance dates per booking
every vendor booking shows the deposit, the balance, the days to the balance date and the saving against the quote, so nothing is paid early or forgotten
Payment check and weekly cash calendar
every vendor payment is on time, late or overdue, and the next 13 weeks show what must go out each week
Cost of a vendor who cancels
the extra cost of the replacement, the deposit lost and the effect on the client price and your margin, with the cancelled bookings listed
the amount in dispute, the days open and the credit to ask for, so a disputed invoice never blocks the rest of the payments
on time, quality and communication for every job give each vendor an average score and a grade, so you rebook the best and watch the weak
quotes with extras, travel and overtime compared on the total, with response days and the saving against the other quotes
every date a vendor holds for you with the days left and a flag when a hold ends within a week
liability insurance and other documents with the days to expiry, a valid, expiring or expired flag and the vendors without cover
for every event the categories planned against the categories booked, so an upcoming event never goes into the last month with a missing vendor
Preferred vendors with a second choice
a first and a second choice for each category and price level with ratings and phones, ready when a vendor cancels
Venue load-in rules and latest load-out
the loading door, access hours, parking, power and house rules of every venue, with the latest load-out time worked out from the curfew
Vendor spend by month and category
twelve categories by month with the share of the month and a three-month average, to see where the money goes

Vendor and venue bookings with deposit and balance
One row per vendor or venue booked for an event: quoted and agreed price, deposit share, balance date and status; deposit and balance amounts, days to the balance date and the saving fill in.
Vendor deposits, balances and refunds with due dates
One row per payment to a vendor or venue: deposit, balance or a refund back to you; days late, days to due, the open amount and the payment check fill in from the dates and the status.
Vendors with bookings, spend and open balance
One row per vendor with price level, rating and payment terms; bookings, spend, open balance, average score, the last booking and whether the vendor is dormant fill in from the other pages.
Venues with events held and spend
One row per venue with capacity, hire fee, minimum spend, curfew and set-up hours; events held, events booked and the venue cost counted from the bookings fill in.
Events with vendors booked and missing categories
One row per event with date, venue, guests, lead and status; vendors booked, committed cost, categories booked against planned and the venue cost fill in from the bookings.
One row per scored booking: on time, quality and communication from 1 to 5 and whether you would rebook; the vendor, the event, the overall score and a grade fill in.
Quote requests with response days and the chosen quote
One row per quote asked from a vendor for an event: when asked, when answered, the price and whether it won; response days, the state, the quotes compared and the saving against the others fill in.
Dates held with vendors and when each hold ends
One row per date a vendor holds for you: who, for which event, until when and whether it was confirmed or released; days left, the expiry check and whether it was handled in time fill in.
Vendor documents and insurance with expiry dates
One row per document a vendor must keep valid, such as liability insurance: expiry and file reference; days to expiry, the month and a valid, expiring or expired flag fill in.
One row per cancelled booking or replaced vendor: who cancelled, why, the replacement and its price, the deposit paid and refunded; days before the event, extra cost and deposit lost fill in.
Disputed vendor invoices with the amount in dispute
One row per disputed vendor invoice: the issue, the amount in dispute, when it was raised, the expected fix and when it was resolved; days open, the state and the vendor fill in.
Vendor payments due and paid by week
One row per week, past and the next 13 weeks: vendor payments due, paid and overdue, the running total of what falls due and the amount due in the next four weeks fill in from the payments.
Preferred vendors by category and price level
One row per category and price level with your first and second choice and a note; the first choice rating and the phone numbers of both choices fill in from the vendor list.
One row per price change a vendor announced: old and new package price and the reason; the category, the change in amount and the change share fill in.
One row per call or message with a vendor: topic, who spoke to them, the outcome and the date of the next step; days since the contact and a follow-up check fill in.
Own rental items with value and payback
One row per item you own and hire out to events: quantity, cost, hire price and events used; the value, the hire income earned and the events needed to pay the item back fill in.
Referral fees agreed with vendors and venues
One row per referral fee or booking commission you agreed to pay a vendor or venue; the event date, whether it is paid and the days it has waited fill in.
Loading access, power and rules at each venue
One row per venue with the loading door, access hours, parking, power and house rules; the curfew comes from Venues and the latest load-out time is worked out from it.
One row per vendor with references checked, insurance on file and contract signed; a complete flag and the days it took to finish the onboarding fill in.
One row per month and vendor category (venue hire is shown on the venue pages): spend paid, bookings made, the share of the month and the three-month average fill in from the payments and bookings.

Hello, please confirm your booking for {event_id} on {event_date}: price {agreed}, deposit {deposit_amt}, balance {balance_amt} due {balance_due}. Thank you.
Hello, we hold your date for {event_id} on {event_date} until {held_until}. We will confirm or release it before then.
Hello, your payment {payment_id} of {amount} for {event_id} was paid on {paid_on}. Please confirm it arrived.
Hello, your balance of {amount} for {event_id} is due on {due_date}. Please send the invoice if you have not yet.
Hello, your balance of {amount} was paid today for {event_id}. Thank you for your work.
Hello, the head count for {event_id} on {event_date} is {guests}. Please confirm the order for that number.
Hello, please confirm your arrival time and loading access for {event_id} at {venue} on {event_date}. We send the venue rules with the schedule.
Hello, your {kind} document expires on {expiry}. Please send the new one before then.
Vendor: your invoice does not match
Hello, your invoice for {payment_id} ({event_id}) does not match the order. Please check it and send a corrected one.
Vendor: we need a revised quote
Hello, we need a revised quote for {event_id} by {reply_by}. Please show extras, travel and overtime separately.
Hello, thank you for {event_id}. Your overall score is {overall} out of 5 ({grade}). We would like to work with you again.
Vendor: we have to cancel the booking
Hello, we have to cancel the booking for {event_id} (cancelled on {cancelled_on}). Please confirm the cancellation and the refund of the deposit.
Hello, please confirm the refund of {deposit_refunded} for the cancelled booking {booking_id}. The deposit paid was {deposit_paid}.

Hello, if our first {category} cannot do an event, can you step in at short notice? Please tell us your price and the notice you need.
Vendor: your referral fee is paid

Hello, the final head count for {date} ({event_id}) is {guests}. Please confirm the room and the set-up.
Hello, the balance of {balance_amt} for {event_id} is due on {balance_due}. Please send the final invoice.
Owner: a vendor cancelled the booking
Hello, {original_vendor} cancelled the booking for {event_id} on {cancelled_on}. I am asking the second choice to step in.
Owner: a vendor balance is overdue
Hello, the payment {payment_id} for {vendor} ({event_id}) is {days_late} days past its due date: {amount} is still open.
Owner: payments to vendors next weeks
Hello, payments to vendors due in the 4 weeks from {week} total {four_wk}. Due in the first week: {due}.
Hello, the {kind} of {vendor} expires on {expiry}. I have asked for the new document.

Hello, the replacement for {original_vendor} costs {extra_cost} more ({extra_share} above the original). Do you agree?
Lead: confirm all vendors this week
Hello, please confirm all vendors of {event_id} ({name}) this week: {vendors_booked} are booked and {missing} categories are still open.

Hello, a vendor invoice for {event_id} is disputed: {amount_disputed} of {amount}. Please send the owner the order and the delivery note.
Hello, please record the vendor scores for {event_id} ({name}) within a week of the event.
Hello, the hold with {vendor} for {event_id} ends on {held_until}. Please confirm or release it before then.
